title: Ratios at Home
subject: math
instructions: Your numbers are different from your neighbor's. Show your work. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.prompt: Unit Price: {{n}} smoothies cost {{money(n*p)}}. How much does 1 smoothie cost?
questions.key: Divides {{money(n*p)}} by {{n}} to get {{money(p)}} for one smoothie.

questions.prompt: Recipe Ratio: A smoothie uses {{a}} cups of mango for every {{b}} cups of yogurt. Fill in the table.
Same Taste? Which recipe tastes the same as {{a}} cups mango to {{b}} cups yogurt?

options.why: Adding the same amount changes the ratio.
That flips the ratio: more mango than yogurt.
Multiply both numbers by the same amount.

questions.prompt: Explain: Leo makes paint with 2 cups blue for every 5 cups white. He uses 6 cups blue. How much white does he need? Explain how you know.
questions.key: 15 cups white: 2 to 6 is times 3, so 5 times 3 is 15. Full credit needs 15 and the times-3 reason; 15 alone is partial.

pool.prompt: Explain: A trail mix has 3 scoops nuts for every 4 scoops raisins. Ana uses 9 scoops nuts. How many scoops of raisins? Explain how you know.
pool.key: 12 scoops: 3 to 9 is times 3, so 4 times 3 is 12. Full credit needs 12 and the times-3 reason; 12 alone is partial.

pool.prompt: Explain: A class has 4 boys for every 5 girls. There are 20 girls. How many boys? Explain how you know.
pool.key: 16 boys: 5 to 20 is times 4, so 4 times 4 is 16. Full credit needs 16 and the times-4 reason; 16 alone is partial.
